:::{#sol-epe-split-noise}

Express the [prediction error](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-error) as [noise](#def-noise) plus the error of the [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction), used as an [estimator](estimation.qmd#def-estimator) of the [mean function](#def-mean-function) value $\truemeanf{\predvar}$:

$$
\ba
\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}
&= \paren{\newoutvar - \truemeanf{\predvar}} + \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(add and subtract } \truemeanf{\predvar} \text{)} \\
&= \noise + \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(definition of } \newoutvar \text{)}
\ea
$$

Square it:

$$
\ba
\sqf{\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}}
&= \noise^2
+ 2 \noise \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}
+ \sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(expand the square of a sum)}
\ea
$$

Take the expectation of each term in turn, using
[linearity of expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-linearity-expectation)
to distribute the expectation over the sum.

For the noise term,
the [variance identity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-variance)
gives $\varpar = \E{\noise^2} - \sqf{\E{\noise}}$:

$$
\ba
\E{\noise^2}
&= \varpar + \sqf{\E{\noise}}
&& \text{(variance identity)} \\
&= \varpar + 0^2
&& \text{(the noise has population mean } 0 \text{)} \\
&= \varpar
&& \text{(} 0^2 = 0 \text{, and } \varpar + 0 = \varpar \text{)}
\ea
$$

For the cross term,
$\noise = \newoutvar - \truemeanf{\predvar}$ shifts $\newoutvar$ by a constant,
and $\newoutvar$ is independent of $\trainset$,
so $\noise$ is independent of $\trainset$,
and hence of $\predvalf{\predvar}$ and of $\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}$.
The expectation of a product of independent random variables is the product of their expectations:

$$
\ba
\E{2 \noise \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}}
&= 2 \E{\noise \paren{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}}
&& \text{(constant factor 2)} \\
&= 2 \E{\noise} \E{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(independence)} \\
&= 2 \cdot 0 \cdot \E{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}
&& \text{(the noise has population mean } 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(zero times a number)}
\ea
$$

Adding the three expectations,

$$
\E{\sqf{\newoutvar - \predvalf{\predvar}}}
= \varpar + \E{\sqf{\truemeanf{\predvar} - \estmeanf{\predvar}}}.
$$ {#eq-epe-after-noise}

The noise has [population mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) $0$ by @thm-noise-mean-zero,
so the algebra used only one hypothesis about the [new observation](#def-new-observation): it is independent of the [training set](#def-training-set).
Independence holds for a fresh observation,
and it fails for an observation the procedure was trained on,
whose noise helped determine the prediction.
It also fails when the new observation depends on the training data
(for example, a later time in the same series),
or when the same [test set](#def-test-set) was used to choose the procedure.

The algebra did not use that the new pair has the same [population distribution](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population-distribution) as the training data.
Suppose the new pair came from a [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population) whose mean function differed from the training population's.
Then @eq-epe-after-noise would still hold, with the new population's mean function and noise variance.
Its [estimation-error](estimation.qmd#def-estimation-error) term would include the [bias](estimation.qmd#def-bias) from that difference.
So it would no longer measure how well the procedure [estimates](estimation.qmd#def-estimate) the training population's mean function.

:::
